proposal: Among its cross-agency requests, the Mandate asks the State Department to quickly impose stiff sanctions on recalcitrant countries until they actually accept deportees, not merely promise to. It asks DOJ either to move the immigration courts to DHS or to treat immigration judges and Board of Immigration Appeals members as national security personnel, decertify their union, and hire significantly more. The same list also covers housing, education, labor, Treasury and intelligence items that this record does not track.

status_summary: Executive Order 14159, section 13 (signed 2025-01-20), directs State and DHS to apply INA section 243(d) visa sanctions to countries that refuse removable nationals; the Laken Riley Act (approved 2025-01-29) lets states sue the Secretary of State over a failure to apply them; and on 2025-04-05 the Secretary of State announced revocation of all visas held by South Sudanese passport holders and a halt to new issuance over South Sudan's failure to accept returns. For the immigration judges' union, the Federal Labor Relations Authority had already excluded immigration judges from their bargaining unit as management officials in 2020 and 2022, before this period; the only later step found is EO 14251 of 2025-03-27, which excludes the Department of Justice as a whole from the federal labor-management relations program without naming EOIR. The outcome of the judges' December 2024 petition to restore the union was not found, and no step moving EOIR to DHS was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14159 was signed; section 13 directs the Secretaries of State and Homeland Security to apply INA section 243(d) sanctions where appropriate and to remove barriers to prompt returns, weighing delayed identity confirmation.

The Laken Riley Act (Public Law 119-1) was approved; section 3(c) adds a subsection to INA section 243 letting a state attorney general sue the Secretary of State for injunctive relief over a failure to discontinue visas as required by section 243(d).

Executive Order 14251 was signed, listing the Department of Justice as a whole among agencies excluded from the federal labor-management relations program; it does not name EOIR or immigration judges.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced revocation of all visas held by South Sudanese passport holders and a halt to further issuance, saying South Sudan's government had not fully accepted timely return of citizens the United States seeks to remove.

The South Sudan statement was read through a hosted copy because state.gov did not load. A Cuban delegation visa denial reported in February 2026 under section 243(d) comes from a tracking site summary of a newspaper report and is not used. For the union element, the decertification events (FLRA 2020 and 2022) predate this period; the only event since 2025-01-20 is EO 14251's DOJ-wide exclusion, which does not name EOIR or immigration judges, and a search found no FLRA ruling on the December 2024 restoration petition. Whether any 2025 DOJ action treats judges as national security personnel was not found.
